title: MTSTRec: Multimodal Time-Aligned Shared Token Recommender
page_convention: 1-based PDF pages; printed paper pages unless explicitly stated otherwise
summary: The printed raw-cosine log objective is undefined on admissible embeddings. Retaining its actual negative sign and inserting a sigmoid still leaves a materially different positive-class weighting in the release. The earlier missing-minus allegation is withdrawn. Separate Minor catalog-selection defect.
supported_impact: Major operative mathematical training definition; no demonstrated historical benchmark decline.

problems.title: The stated optimization objective is undefined on allowed embeddings and differs materially from the released loss
problems.source_claim: Section 3.4, PDF p.6, defines cos(z_output,y^k) as ordinary cosine similarity. Eq.(8) has the conventional NEGATIVE prefactor -1/|K_gt union K_n|. It omits a sigmoid, another probability conversion, a positivity restriction and positive-class reweighting, and is stated to drive training. The minus is visible in the reliable PyMuPDF recovery rendering of the same original page.
assumptions: Nonzero real output and item vectors, the domain needed for ordinary cosine similarity; no nonnegativity condition is imposed.
A positive-item set and negative-item set with disjoint item identities; distinct items may have coinciding learned embeddings because no injectivity condition is imposed.
For the source comparison P=|K_gt|>0 and N=|K_n|; the default N=100 is explicit in parameters.py line72, and P=2 is allowed by the multi-label task.

For the unweighted-versus-source minimizer comparison, retain the printed conventional negative sign and insert a sigmoid probability link; this comparator repairs the cosine-domain defect but not the released class weighting.
problems.complete_check: For unit vectors z=(1,0), y_positive=(-1/2,sqrt(3)/2), and y_negative=(1/2,sqrt(3)/2), the cosine scores are -1/2 and +1/2. All vectors are nonzero and normalized and can be embedded in any larger feature space; no original domain condition is violated. Eq.(8) then includes log(-1/2), which is undefined as a real training loss. After retaining the printed negative sign and inserting sigmoid scores, the repaired unweighted BCE has the finite value log(1+exp(1/2))=0.974076984... for this one-positive/one-negative illustration. Static trainer.py lines213-232 shows sigmoid(cos) and an additional factor N/P multiplying the summed positive log terms. The source implements L_src= -[(N/P)sum_pos log sigma(c_k)+sum_neg log(1-sigma(c_k))]/(P+N). Retaining the printed negative sign and inserting sigma in Eq.(8) gives the charitable repaired comparator L_unw= -[sum_pos log sigma(c_k)+sum_neg log(1-sigma(c_k))]/(P+N), a different objective. To prove non-equivalence, choose P=2, N=100, all item embeddings equal a unit vector y, and output z(c) a unit vector with dot product c in [-1,1]; this is allowed because no distinctness restriction is placed on embeddings. Then dL_unw/dc=sigma(c)-2/102>0 throughout [-1,1] (sigma(-1)>2/102), so its unique constrained minimum is c=-1. In contrast dL_src/dc=(100/102)(2sigma(c)-1), giving a unique minimum c=0. Thus even the favorable sigmoid-link repair does not describe the released optimization problem. The comparison uses the actual printed negative sign; the original raw-cosine domain defect and the additional released reweighting are separate.
problems.counterevidence: The published equation already has a conventional negative sign; the previous contrary reading was caused by a missing glyph in the initial raster and is withdrawn. The source applies the negative sign at trainer.py232 and sigmoids at214-215, so this check does not imply released training produces NaNs. An implicit sigmoid interpretation would repair the domain but conflicts with the explicit ordinary-cosine definition and still omits positive reweighting. If P=N, the weight is one; the multi-answer task with N=100 does not require P=N. The complete embedding-to-loss path uses LayerNorm followed by unconstrained affine representation layers (model.py64,75,86,102,111; applied255-265 before concatenation267), with the same affine maps for item embeddings at trainer.py183-194. No final positivity constraint precedes CosineSimilarity at trainer.py62,213. Recovery source-page inspection confirms the negative prefactor, ordinary cosine definition, and lack of sigmoid and class weights.
problems.impact: This concerns the operative mathematical definition used to train the proposed recommender, not a peripheral prose claim: the displayed objective fails on its allowed domain and does not identify the source's training criterion even after the charitable sigmoid-link repair. On the user's core-contribution calibration, recommend Major for this central method-definition defect, while explicitly preserving the empirical and architectural conclusions not refuted by it. No empirical benchmark score reduction is established or required for the mathematical discrepancy. The parent retained Major after the focused source, domain and dependency check; the rejected missing-minus allegation is not part of its basis.
problems.correction: A source-aligned corrected statement is the weighted sigmoid BCE formula L_src above, for nonzero embeddings and P,N>0. The analytic check shows it is finite for cosine scores and matches the static weighting structure for one sequence. This is not a claim that this was the historical experimental loss. If the intended method is instead ordinary unweighted sigmoid BCE, the source must be reconciled and experimental provenance supplied; fresh training may be necessary to determine the difference.
evidence: papers/0157/0157.pdf §3.4 Eq.(8) p.6; Appendix G pp.16-17

normalization_audit.paper_location: p6 before Eq7 says final modality representations are normalized
normalization_audit.conclusion: LayerNorm is followed by unrestricted affine representation layers; item vectors use the same unrestricted affine maps. No final positivity constraint was found. Unit normalization, even if imposed independently, preserves the sign of cosine.
normalization_audit.stronger_optional_construction: If one additionally demands zero-mean unit vectors, take z=(1,-1,0)/sqrt(2), v=(1,1,-2)/sqrt(6), and y_positive=-(1/2)z+(sqrt(3)/2)v. Then z and y_positive are zero-mean unit vectors and their cosine is -1/2. Scaling by sqrt(3) gives unit coordinate variance if desired without changing cosine. This is a mathematical construction, not an author-code execution.

focused_correction.change: Withdraw missing-minus allegation; original Eq.(8) is negative. Domain and class-weight arguments and all numerical results are unchanged.

problems.title: The released negative sampler overwrites the contemporaneous product catalog
problems.source_claim: Appendix O.4, p.21, states that monthly product lists are beginning-of-month availability snapshots used with purchase dates to determine which products can be offered. mainfinal.py lines116-135 loads lists in sorted filename order; dataloader.py lines33-39 converts their keys to corresponding first-of-month dates. The sampler comments that it selects the candidate products during the purchase date (lines201-209), but its loop overwrites the selection through the final month.
assumptions: Monthly snapshots have increasing dates, as produced by sorted YYMM filenames and preserved dictionary insertion order.
Purchase date lies after the first snapshot and before a later snapshot.
There are at least 100 unseen candidates in each relevant example pool, with no duplicates; positive item IDs and browsing-history IDs are excluded as the sampler requires.
The diagnosis is for the pinned source; no claim is made that this exact source produced the paper's experiments.
problems.complete_check: Let snapshots be dated 2024-01-01, 2024-02-01, 2024-03-01, and purchase date 2024-02-15. Give each snapshot common IDs1,2,3,4 plus 100 unique month-specific IDs: January101..200, February201..300, March301..400. Let history=[1,2,3], positive set=[4], N=100 and seed79. All purchased/history items exist in each catalog and every catalog has exactly 100 eligible negatives. At k=0, buydate>January sets candidateproducts=monthproduct[-1], i.e. March. At k=1, buydate>February sets monthproduct[0], January. At final k=2, the condition buydate<=ym and k!=last is false because k=last; buydate>March is false; the else assigns March again. The final pool is March301..400, while the correct contemporaneous snapshot is February201..300. With 100 unique negatives drawn from 100 eligible IDs, the pool discrepancy is deterministic even though no random author sampler was executed. More generally, the final iteration alone yields the last snapshot for t<=last_date, and the penultimate snapshot for t>last_date, independently of intervening dates.
problems.counterevidence: If every month has identical item membership, this bug is dormant. If the intended evaluation deliberately uses a fixed global catalog, no temporal lookup is needed, but that is not the stated monthly-availability convention and does not explain the penultimate-month behavior after the last date. Missing historical source provenance prevents attributing numerical benchmark damage. This is separate from the TST module's relative positional alignment and does not refute its attention-mask design.
problems.impact: The pinned implementation can train/evaluate against products not yet available and omit contemporaneous products, changing the negative-sampling task. Classify the demonstrated release-level defect Minor, leaving paper-score impact Needs Evidence until the actual original pools and experimental source version are known. Do not infer a direction or magnitude of performance bias.
problems.correction: For sorted snapshot dates d_0<...<d_{M-1} and a session t>=d_0, select j=max{i:d_i<=t} once, then use catalog_j. Explicitly handle sessions before d_0 and insufficient eligible negatives. This selects February for the finite example and can be proved from the definition of beginning-of-month snapshots; historical benchmark changes require replaying original sampling/evaluation.
